prize_parts.citation: for the development of targeted protein degradation, in which designed bifunctional small molecules direct ubiquitin ligases to chosen proteins

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: B020 as the whole prize, with Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli. After reading all eight round-1 statements, I think the scientific case is stronger than it was at opening, because six members now describe the same mechanism independently: a designed small molecule forms a ligase-target ternary complex and replaces occupancy-based inhibition with event-driven, catalytic removal of the protein. That is a chemical principle that can be stated in one sentence and has been reproduced widely. I weigh the third seat on what the citation says. A citation about designed degraders is carried by Crews and Deshaies, who conceived the bifunctional approach, and by Ciulli, whose structure-guided VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures and cooperativity measurements made degrader design a rational, transferable discipline. The first-generation PROTACs were peptidic and barely usable as drugs. A single-principle citation of this kind answers the chair's question about wording without implying that Handa, Ito, Gray, Sakamoto or Kim did not contribute.
statement.case_against: No PROTAC drug is approved, and the committee must accept that the prize rests on concept, structural and mechanistic work and independent reproduction, with clinical outcomes still ahead. The three-person limit also leaves out real claimants: Handa and Ito for cereblon, Gray for degrader and glue chemistry, and Sakamoto and Kim as first authors of the 2001 paper. Choosing Ciulli over Handa is a judgment about which story the citation tells, and four colleagues judge it the other way. A skeptical reader could also say that this is medicinal chemistry that Medicine might claim, and that a mature prize such as B061 would carry less risk.

responses.point: Linke asks why Car-Parrinello should be preferred now and not in a later year, and argues that degraders have had no recognition while computational methods were recognised in 2013 and 2024. He proposes Crews, Deshaies and Handa, with a citation covering both PROTACs and cereblon.
responses.response: His question is fair and I answer it by moving B061 down: I do not claim it must go in 2026. Car and Parrinello will be as deserving next year as they are now, whereas the degrader field is at a point where its founding concepts are clear and the committee can still credit the right people. On the third seat, I do not accept that cereblon makes the glue strand the same achievement as designed bifunctional degraders. Handa's identification of cereblon explains drugs that were found empirically, while the PROTAC lineage is about design. Joining them in one citation gives a compromise that your own case-against statement already calls a possible compromise between two prizes. I would sooner have a narrower citation that is exactly true. If the committee insists on the glue strand, I would accept Handa only if the citation says so explicitly and if the committee accepts that it is then crediting two lineages, which is a different prize from the one I am proposing.

responses.point: Chabes asks whether Car-Parrinello is more defensible than degradation given the 2013 and 2024 computational prizes, and proposes a two-part prize with Liu alone for base editing and Crews and Deshaies for degradation.
responses.response: I do not think B061 is more defensible than B020 this year, so it does not displace a biology-facing part, and I do not press it. On the two-part configuration, I agree that Liu alone is the only clean attribution for base editing and that its mechanism, deamination on a single-stranded R-loop with an evolved adenine deaminase, is chemically distinct. My difficulty is the 2020 prize and the Kondo and Nishida priority claim for cytidine deamination, which Linke and Somfai also raise and which nobody has resolved. A two-part prize also forces B020 down to two names and removes the third place that I think Ciulli should have. I prefer to keep base editing as an alternative and revisit it once the priority question is settled.

responses.point: Brzezinski gives B020 as the strongest well-defined proposal in this round, but worries that it is a medicinal chemistry and pharmacology achievement that Medicine could claim, and asks whether the unresolved mechanism of nitrogenase affects maturity.
responses.response: I take the Medicine concern seriously, and I think the citation should answer it by naming the chemical principle: induced proximity between a ligase and a target through a ternary complex, designed with small molecules. Ternary-complex cooperativity, linker design and ligand optimisation against a ligase are physical-organic and structural chemistry, and that is why Ciulli's contribution belongs in the prize. The wording I propose says designed bifunctional small molecules for this reason. On nitrogenase, an unresolved detail of substrate reduction does not by itself make a discovery immature. The cofactor structure and the Rees, Einsle and Seefeldt work are settled. My difficulty with B028 remains the crowded credit and the lack of support beyond your own ranking.

responses.point: Sparr argues that Crews and Deshaies's concept and Handa's cereblon work explain two complementary halves of one mechanism, so that three people can honestly cover both, and that B061 is better kept for a later year.
responses.response: I agree on B061 and I have moved accordingly. I do not agree that the two halves are one mechanism in the sense a citation needs. The ternary complex is shared, but in the glue case the molecule remodels the surface of an existing ligase to bind a neosubstrate, discovered after the fact, whereas the PROTAC is built from two separate ligands joined by a linker. The chemistry of design, which is what I am arguing for, is different in the two cases. I also note your point that the case against B020 includes this very compromise. That is why my citation is limited to bifunctional degraders.

responses.point: Aili moved his third name from Ciulli to Handa because five colleagues proposed Handa, and he says the cereblon discovery turns thalidomide-type drugs from a clinical accident into a mechanistically understood class. He also says our disagreement on B061 concerns order and not merit.
responses.response: I agree that the disagreement about B061 is about order and I have conceded the order. On Handa, I respect the argument that cereblon turned an accident into a mechanism, and it is the strongest point in favour of the glue lineage. I do not think five colleagues naming Handa is a scientific reason, and I would not want the third seat decided by how many people wrote the same name. The question is whether the prize is for the design of degraders or for understanding how thalidomide works. For the first, Ciulli is the better third name. If the committee prefers the second, Handa is the correct name, but then Deshaies's role needs to be reconsidered, and I would want us to say that openly.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept Ciulli, and not Handa, as the third name, and whether any single citation can span both the bifunctional and cereblon glue lineages without becoming a compromise.
Whether the absence of an approved PROTAC drug makes a 2026 award premature; I regard it as tolerable, and early approvals or late-stage trial failures would change my view of the timing.
Whether I have the exact priority dates for the 2001 PROTAC paper, the VHL ligand work and the cereblon identification right, since I am relying on memory and have not checked them.
Whether the Kondo and Nishida claim for cytidine deamination would affect an attribution for base editing, which I list only as an alternative.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict has changed since round 1. I know of no tie to Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli or any other person on B020, B061 or B047. My postdoctoral collaboration with Arieh Warshel on EVB is not relevant to any shortlisted ballot. My work in biomolecular simulation is in the same broad field as Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics, but I have no personal tie to Car or Parrinello, and B061 is not in my preferred configuration. I have served on the committee with Peter Brzezinski since 2015 and do not regard it as a recusal issue.
